questions.q: In this case study, what two separate questions does Priya have to keep apart when the VP pushes back?
options: Whether the finding is in scope versus how technically severe the authentication bypass is
Whether the client paid the invoice versus whether the report is late
Whether Priya likes the client versus whether she trusts the IT director
Whether the tool she used was Nmap or Metasploit
questions.explain: A scoping fact (was it in the original scope document) is completely separate from a technical fact (how severe the vulnerability actually is), and business pressure can only legitimately affect the first.

questions.q: Why doesn't documenting the claims-processing finding as an 'out-of-scope discovery' excuse lowering its severity rating?
options: Severity ratings automatically reset to Medium for anything found outside the original scope
Scope status and technical severity are independent facts -- the finding is reported honestly as out-of-scope AND still flagged at its full, actual severity
Out-of-scope findings are never included in the final report at all
The VP's business concerns override the CVSS score once a contract renewal is involved
questions.explain: One doesn't cancel the other: the report is honest about the scope boundary while still rating the finding by what it technically is.

questions.q: What is Lesson 1's escalation procedure used for in this case study?
options: Scheduling the next penetration test automatically
Only for findings that are explicitly in the original scope document
Formally raising a serious finding through the ROE's named, documented channel, instead of letting informal pushback settle it over email
Generating the CVSS score for a finding
questions.explain: The engagement lead uses the documented emergency contact and escalation path the ROE already named, rather than treating the VP's informal pushback as the final word.

questions.q: What does this lesson say a tester should do if a client insists a validated Critical finding be deleted from the report entirely?
options: Quietly comply, since the client is the one paying for the engagement
Decline the request, and decline it in writing, since a tester's integrity to the findings outranks a client's comfort with them
Lower the severity to Medium as a compromise
Remove the finding but mention it verbally during the closeout call
questions.explain: Professional ethics codes referenced throughout this course place accurate reporting above a client's comfort with an inconvenient result.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real test of a professional penetration tester in a case like this one?
options: Whether they can find more vulnerabilities than a competing firm
Whether they can finish the engagement faster than the agreed testing window
Whether they avoid any conversation that might upset a client stakeholder
Whether the report that leaves the building still says what the testing actually found, regardless of who preferred otherwise
questions.explain: Finding vulnerabilities is the easy part; keeping the report accurate under real pushback is what separates professional work from a service that just tells clients what they want to hear.
